result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.find_cohesive_blocks()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Find hierarchical cohesive block structure. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L20931-L20997){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.find_cohesive_blocks() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Cohesive blocks](/assets/graphs/algo-cohesive-blocks.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="A nine-node graph organized as three nested tiers of cohesion. A dense inner triangle of three accent nodes forms the innermost cohesive block; four accent-lite nodes in the middle tier each attach to the core; two default peripheral nodes at the far sides sit in the outermost tier." width="100%"} Identifies k-cohesive blocks in the graph, where a k-cohesive block is a maximal subgraph that requires removal of at least `k` nodes to disconnect it. Returns a hierarchical structure where child blocks have higher cohesion than their parents. Time complexity: `O(V^5)` due to node connectivity computations. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[list[int]], list[int], list[int | None]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A tuple containing: (1) blocks, a list of node sets (each as list of node IDs), (2) cohesion, a list of k-values (cohesion of each block), and (3) parent, a list of parent block indices (`None` for root blocks). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A complete graph `K_5` is a single maximally cohesive block, since every node connects directly to every other: ::: {#79ccacab .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() for i in range(1, 6): graph.add_node(label=str(i)) for i in range(1, 6): for j in range(i + 1, 6): graph.add_edge(str(i), str(j)) blocks, cohesions, parents = graph.find_cohesive_blocks() # Returns ([[1, 2, 3, 4, 5]], [4], [None]) (blocks, cohesions, parents) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ([[3, 1, 5, 4, 2]], [4], [None]) ``` ::: ::: Attaching a smaller, less-cohesive component to a dense core reveals a hierarchical structure: the outer graph forms a weaker root block, while the dense `K_4` core forms a more cohesive child block nested inside it: ::: {#2b37b275 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() for i in range(1, 5): graph.add_node(label=str(i)) for i in range(1, 5): for j in range(i + 1, 5): graph.add_edge(str(i), str(j)) graph.add_node(label="5") graph.add_node(label="6") graph.add_edge("1", "5") graph.add_edge("2", "5") graph.add_edge("5", "6") graph.add_edge("6", "1") graph.add_edge("6", "2") blocks, cohesions, parents = graph.find_cohesive_blocks() # The K_4 sub-block (cohesion 3) is nested under the weaker root block (blocks, cohesions, parents) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ([[3, 1, 5, 6, 4, 2], [3, 4, 1, 2], [5, 6, 1, 2]], [2, 3, 3], [None, 0, 0]) ``` ::: :::
